source_title: Spain train crash: Videos capture overturned carriages, passengers, devastation
source_excerpt: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spainâs central province of Toledo. Videos and photographs from the scene showed overturned carriages, injured passengers and emergency crews working to rescue people trapped in the wreckage.The collision occurred on Wednesday morning near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville rail route. Recordings captured by passengers showed scenes inside the trains following the impact, while images from the site showed carriages lying on their sides beside the tracks.Emergency services rushed to the scene to evacuate passengers, provide medical assistance and search the wreckage for survivors. Injured passengers were taken to nearby medical facilities, including a sports centre converted into a temporary treatment site. The regional government of Castilla-La Mancha said 58 people were receiving treatment in hospitals.According to Spainâs rail infrastructure operator ADIF, both trains were travelling south from Madrid towards Seville when the collision occurred. Puente said the train was authorised to continue under circumstances that investigators would need to examine.âThere was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed,â Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday. âIt is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.âThe RENFE train reportedly resumed its journey at about 124 miles per hour before hitting the stationary IRYO train.
